Yesterday I started a thread to compile info on the theory that Germanic-speaking peoples lived natively in Britain since the Bronze Age. Today I came across a similar theory: that the ancient Aryans were not nomadic invaders in 1500 BC, but urban-dwellers already settled in India at least by 2000 BC. Thus, according to this theory, no Aryan "invasion" is needed to explain the presence of Aryan culture in India, and the narrative of Dravidians being replaced is inaccurate.

Three Indian proponents of this theory are Professor Dipak Basu, Ramesh Chandra Mazumdar, and archaeologists Rakhaldas Banerjee and S.P.Gupta, all of whom contest the alleged evidence of a conquering Aryan invasion. According to Professor Basu, "Russian archeologists and linguists also proved that the Aryans have migrated not from the Russian steppes but came to Russia via Armenia and Georgia. There are increasing evidence that India was the original home of the Aryans."

Professor Basu points to the discovery of Arkaim, an archaeological site in Russia thought to have belonged to a culture contemporary with ancient Egypt, with a very elaborate, pre-planned urban design that followed a swastika-like pattern. The area of southwest Russia where Arkaim is located was thus an earlier home to sophisticated urban civilization than previously believed. The predominant narrative has been that the steppes of Russia going into Central Asia were nothing but untamed expanses constantly raided by nomadic warrior tribes on horseback since at least the time of the ancient Greeks, first by Scythians, and later by Huns and Mongols.

President Putin has recently visited one of the most mysterious places on planet Earth - the ruins of the ancient town of Arkaim, which is situated on the outskirts of the city of Chelyabinsk. Pravda reported (on 16 July 2005) about the starling discovery of ruins of a very advanced civilization of Indo-Aryan origin, which was at least 4000 years old in Arkaim.

The Arkaim valley in the south of Ural was supposed to be flooded in 1987; local authorities were going to create a water reservoir there to irrigate droughty fields. However, scientists found strange circles in the center of the valley: the authorities gave archaeologists time to explore the area. Scientists were shocked to find out that Arkaim was the same age as Egypt and Babylon. Archaeological excavations showed that the people, who inhabited Arkaim, represented the ancient Indo-Aryan civilizations. Arkaim had not only a city, but also a temple and an astronomic observatory.

How far is Iran from Sindh-Saraswati valley? We also know from the Purana, that Aryans were divided into two groups, Sur of India and Asura of Iran. If they would know, it would be possible to prove what Rakhaldas Banerjee; Ramesh Chadra Mazumdar said all along that India was the origin of the ancient Aryans, who had migrated to Russia via Armenia. The discovery made by the Russian archeologists of the temple of Mithra under the basement of the world’s oldest official Christian church in Yerevan, Armenia shows that link.

Hey Voat. Some of you might recognize me. I comment somewhat frequently, though I only post occasionally. Today I decided to leave Voat, and I thought I'd share my thoughts, in case anyone was interested.

I saw a post on v/suicideanon the other day. It was a 15 year old kid who decided they were going to take their own life. I don't know if that was a true story, or if they really killed themselves or not. From the story they posted, it didn't sound to me like anything Voat had to say significantly contributed to their depression, but it got me thinking about life more generally and how I am spending it.

I don't hate Jews. I recognize the corrosive effects that their communities have had on our nations, and I am strongly against that. I stand against the Talmudic view of the world, and am strongly against how the Jewish ruling elite have been running this world. I want self-determination for my own people, and am willing to fight to get it. But I don't hate the Jews.

I don't hate fat people. I think the obesity epidemic is a symptom of a degenerating culture. I think the denial of science, the denial of common sense and common experience, the denial of self-responsibility, and the need to spew such self-destructive garbage all over the mainstream culture as pro-fat movements are doing is deplorable. I feel disgust when I see someone who has utterly destroyed their one vessel through which to experience and interact with this life. I feel pity and outrage when I see them foisting such a terrible life on their children. But I don't hate fat people.

I don't hate black people. I see the disparity in crime rates. I see the dumbing down of our schools to serve the lowest common denominator. I see the damage and corruption perpetuated by the welfare plantation. I see how the push to integrate vastly different peoples under one government has only led to a lack of useful representation for all, and inevitable conflict. But I don't hate black people.

I don't hate Muslims. I don't hate the Left. I don't hate the Globalists. I see how their ideology is holding back this world, creating war where none is beneficial, and keeping the peace of enslavement where a conflict needs to be sorted out. I see the greed, the malice, the ignorance, the disdain. But I don't hate them.

What I want is for people to see the damage they're doing to the world - the world that they and their descendants have to live in also. What I want is for people to see the Hell they are imposing on others and perpetuating in themselves. And I know that won't solve all our differences. I'd like a situation, for example, where the Jewish community could thrive and be happy by using their particular traits and tendencies in a social structure that benefits from it, while not being corrosive to those around them. I want, for example, fat people to overcome their addictions and find meaning in pursuing health, rather than pushing acceptance of their self-destruction. I want us all to be better individuals, better communities, better nations, a better species.

But I am not some utopian idealist. I understand that, realistically, finding our way to a better future is often going to require separation, evolution, and conflict. And conflict - even bloody, terrible conflict - is part of the rules of the game of Nature, and that is probably something we'll have to continue to contend with. I love my family, and I feel hatred at the thought of them being damaged and destroyed. Sometimes hate is righteous, and even a useful emotion. It's there for a reason.

But it's not good to live in it. It's not useful to dwell there, to be constantly surrounded by it, to live in places where almost nothing can exist without a tinge of hatred.

...

That being said, I'm extremely grateful to have experienced Voat. This place gave me an opportunity to clarify my thoughts through articulation - thoughts which couldn't have been as clearly articulated or engaged nearly anywhere else on the internet. I also learned a lot from the community here. Over the last almost 2 years, I've been presented with many ideas that have helped reshape my perspective. I've been presented with information that gave me a clearer idea of what is happening in the world - again in contexts that are generally not allowed to exist on the internet anymore. I'm thankful to the people here, and I'm thankful that this place exists for others who need to be exposed to these ideas and facts.

So, thank you Voat, for being you. And thank you for taking the time to read this, if you bothered to make it this far. I wish the best for this website. It's just time for me to move on and focus on other things.
